harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Installed Apache httpd on node1 (RHEL 7.9) and configured it to serve a small inventory application on TCP port 8181 (VirtualHost + DocumentRoot /var/www/inventory) while SELinux remained in Enforcing mode throughout. Relabeled the SELinux port context for 8181 from intermapper_port_t to http_port_t via `semanage port -m`, set httpd_sys_content_t on the content directory via `semanage fcontext`/`restorecon`, and opened 8181/tcp in firewalld. Verified the service serves content locally and via NODE_IP with no AVC denials. Performed the mandatory single-node restart: captured baseline boot_id/enforcing status/service state, issued `shutdown -r now`, confirmed disconnect, polled until reachable, and proved a new boot_id/boot time plus full recovery (SELinux Enforcing, httpd active and listening on 8181, inventory content served, firewall port persisted).
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS/SELinux/firewall state (RHEL 7.9, SELinux enforcing, firewalld running, no inventory app present)
Enabled a CentOS 7.9 vault yum repo (no subscription-manager repos enabled) and installed policycoreutils-python, net-tools, httpd
Created /var/www/inventory/index.html inventory content and /etc/httpd/conf.d/inventory.conf VirtualHost on port 8181
Set httpd_sys_content_t SELinux context on /var/www/inventory via semanage fcontext + restorecon
Modified SELinux port context: semanage port -m -t http_port_t -p tcp 8181 (was intermapper_port_t), verified with semanage port -l -C
Opened 8181/tcp permanently in firewalld and reloaded
Enabled and started httpd; verified listening on 8181 and content served via 127.0.0.1 and NODE_IP with SELinux Enforcing and no relevant AVC denials
Captured baseline boot_id and service/data health, issued `shutdown -r now` on node1, confirmed connection drop (ack returned before disconnect)

Polled node1 until exec succeeded again, confirmed new boot_id and new boot timestamp (2026-08-26 -> 2026-09-04), and verified post-restart recovery of SELinux Enforcing, httpd active, port 8181 listening, inventory content served, and firewall rule persisted

evidence.requirement: Baseline: SELinux enforcing, port 8181 present but not yet http-usable, no inventory app running
evidence.summary: Confirmed RHEL 7.9, SELINUX=enforcing in /etc/selinux/config and /sys/fs/selinux/enforce=1, and no pre-existing inventory app/listener on node1

evidence.requirement: SELinux port context correctly maps 8181 to http_port_t (mandatory access control satisfied, not bypassed)
evidence.summary: semanage port -m -t http_port_t -p tcp 8181 applied; semanage port -l -C shows the local customization http_port_t tcp 8181

evidence.requirement: Inventory application actually serves over TCP 8181 while SELinux stays Enforcing
evidence.summary: httpd active and listening on :::8181; getenforce=Enforcing; curl to 127.0.0.1:8181 and $NODE_IP:8181 both return the inventory HTML content

evidence.requirement: No SELinux denials caused by the port/service configuration (enforcing mode not just nominally on)
evidence.summary: dmesg avc log shows only unrelated denials (pam_tally2, dbus policyload notices); nothing tied to httpd or port 8181
Captured pre-restart boot_id 73bafeef-b823-49b3-8e3d-17981e865b31 and boot time 2026-08-26 10:36:02

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement returned before disconnect
evidence.summary: Backgrounded `shutdown -r now` acknowledged and returned before the SSH connection was closed by the reboot

evidence.requirement: node1 boot identity changed after restart (proof of actual reboot, not just service restart)
evidence.summary: Exec calls timed out while node1 was down, then succeeded again; post-restart boot_id f7f1a0ff-d82d-44da-985a-05c59bc7f179 differs from baseline and boot time changed to 2026-09-04 23:32

evidence.requirement: node1 post-restart recovery of required service/data/config
evidence.summary: After restart: SELinux still Enforcing, httpd active and listening on 8181, inventory HTML served correctly via NODE_IP, and firewalld still exposes 8181/tcp
